title: Technology Sector Update for 11/26/2018: NVDA,JKS,DTRM,IPAS
text:

Technology stocks continued to firm this afternoon, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 adding over 2.1% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped more than 1.8%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) NVIDIA Corp ( NVDA ) climbed as much as 5% on Monday after analysts at Credit Suisse initiated coverage of the imaging and gaming semiconductors company with an Outperform investment recommendation and also established a $225 price target. The move follows NVIDIA last Wednesday announcing separate agreements with three Chinese startups to work on new autonomous driving technologies. According to a Reuters report, NVIDIA, together with XPeng Motors and Singulato Motors, expect to use NVIDIA's computing platform and its Xavier driving chip to develop autonomous driving hardware. The company and SF Motors are slated to work on developing a next-generation autonomous driving platform.
In other sector news:
(+) JinkoSolar ( JKS ) raced over 20% higher at one point on Monday after the photovoltaic panels company reported improved Q3 financial results compared with year-ago levels. Excluding one-time items, the company earned RMB5.28, or about $0.76, per American depositary share, up from RMB0.76 per ADS during the same quarter last year and crushing the Capital IQ consensus call expecting a $0.15 per ADS adjusted profit, if comparable. Revenue grew to RMB6.69 billion, or about $974.8 million, from RMB6.42 billion last year and also topping the $934.7 million analyst mean.
(+) Determine ( DTRM ) popped over 3% higher on Monday after the software-as-a-service company said European roofing supplier VM Building Solutions has been managing all of its direct and indirect procurement orders on the company's Determine Cloud Platform since April. VM Building began rollout of the procurement, financial management and invoice processing system in France and Belgium, the companies said, and has now placed over 20,000 orders by over 200 individual users.
(-) iPass ( IPAS ) was falling over 6% despite signing a seven-figure deal to license its iPass SmartConnect Wi-Fi connectivity systems to German telecommunications firm Deutsche Telekom. The companies also are planning to expand their existing relationship to work on creating a dedicated "platform-on-demand" using iPass Smart and managed by Deutsche Telekom as a private cloud.
